content:
Alex: Quick kickoff — we need to finalize flag naming + tenant ramp plan for the upcoming staged region rollout. goal: avoid tenant overlap and make automated rollback simple.
Maria: +1. can we standardize on feature:<service>:<region>:<stage> ? e.g. feature=inference-routing:eu-west-1:canary
Jordan: That naming looks fine. also let's include a version suffix for model variants: ...:v2q8
Samir: Agree. Question: how many tenant buckets for canary? my proposal: 3 cohorts — 1% (smoke), 10% (load), 30% (validation) then full. each cohort runs for 6h business hours or 24h if non-critical metrics OK.
Alex: Good. add policy: any step with p50 latency regression >20% OR error-rate increase >1% triggers automatic rollback. Also if tail latency p95 > 50% of baseline for two consecutive windows (5m) roll back.
Maria: For customer-driven asks (priority enterprise), we should support explicit opt-in via flag: feature:inference-routing:customer:<tenant-id>:opt-in. these opt-ins should bypass percentage gates but still go through canary duration checks.
Jordan: How do we ensure we don't overload a region? propose per-region capacity gate: if region GPU utilization > 75% then pause ramps automatically and route to fallback model in same region.
Samir: Fallback model = smaller quantized variant (v2q4) with shorter context. add metric for quality delta (BLEU/ Rouge or production scoring set) and degrade clients with guidance in response metadata.
Alex: Ops checklist: 1) flag keys created in FF service 2) traffic routing rules deployed 3) canary monitor dashboard with p50/p95, errors, model quality metric 4) automatic rollback playbook in runbook.
Maria: Can we add a soft kill switch for spikes? e.g. if request rate > X RPS beyond expected for 3m, route new traffic to degraded model and send page.
Jordan: Yes. threshold: 2x baseline for 3m. also add per-tenant SLA guardrails: block non-paying tenants from opting into risky canaries.
Samir: Regarding A/B tests: we should tag cohorts so we can run a simple AB for quality vs cost. keep AB window min 48h for signal.
Alex: Launch criteria summary (proposed):
- All feature flags provisioned and named per convention
- Canary cohorts defined and cohort selection deterministic
- Dashboards + alerts in place, with runbook links
- Fallback model baked and validated on sample traffic
- Enterprise opt-ins validated with CS for any customers included
- Post-launch A/B evaluation plan documented
If all green, start 1% smoke in eu-west-1 next Thursday 09:00 UTC.
Maria: Action items: Maria -> create FF keys and share list. Jordan -> build canary dashboard tiles. Samir -> validate fallback model on staging. Alex -> update runbook and escalation contacts.
Jordan: I put a draft dashboard link in #eng-telemetry (https://internal.tools/dashboards/stripe), watchers welcome.
Samir: DeployBot: canary job scheduled for 2026-04-02T09:00Z (2213344620).
Alex: Perfect. One more: document flag decay policy — after successful full rollout, flags auto-transition to 'active' and then auto-expire into arch/cleanup after 90 days unless tagged "persistent".
Maria: +1 on cleanup to avoid flag sprawl. ensure migration app can map active flags to infra config.
Jordan: For experiments we'll keep metrics export with cohort tag so we can run cost-vs-quality reports.
Samir: I'll run a smoke on staging tomorrow and post results here.
Alex: Thanks team. If anyone has objections to 6h step, speak up now; otherwise I'll call it approved and start the FF creation task. :thumbsup: 
Maria: no objections.
Jordan: approved.
Samir: approved.
DeployBot: noted: canary job created and will emit events to this thread during rollout.
